t.4.44.2: Rāma, together with Lakṣmaṇa, dwelt on that Mount Prasravaṇa, awaiting the month that had been fixed for the finding of Sītā.
t.4.44.1: Having understood that stern command of their master, the foremost of the monkeys set out, covering the earth like locusts.
t.4.44.3: Then the heroic monkey Śatabali set out at once toward the lovely northern direction, which is encompassed by the king of mountains.
t.4.44.4: Vinata, the leader of the monkey troops, set out toward the eastern direction.
t.4.44.6: Suṣeṇa, lord of the monkeys, a tiger among the apes, set out swiftly toward the dreadful western direction guarded by Varuṇa.
t.4.44.5: The monkey, son of the Wind and leader of the monkey troops, accompanied by Tāra, Aṅgada and others, was bound for the southern quarter frequented by Agastya.
t.4.44.7: Then the king, having duly dispatched the foremost commanders of the monkey army to all the directions, rejoiced, happy and at ease.
t.4.44.8: Thus urged by the king, all the leaders of the monkey troops set out in haste, each heading toward his own assigned direction.
t.4.44.9: Roaring, bellowing aloud, thundering and shrieking, the monkeys, the best of leaping creatures, set off at a run, crying: "We shall bring back Sītā and we shall slay Rāvaṇa!"
t.4.44.10: Alone I shall slay Rāvaṇa when he meets me in battle, and then, crushing all resistance by force, I shall carry off the daughter of Janaka.
t.4.44.12: I shall scatter the trees, I shall split the mountains; I shall rend the earth and churn up the oceans.
t.4.44.11: Saying to the one trembling with exhaustion, “Let all of you stay here today,” I alone will bring back Jānakī, even from Pātāla.
t.4.44.13: I am a leaper across distances reckoned in yojanas; of this there is no doubt. A hundred by the count of yojanas, indeed even more than a hundred, can I leap.
t.4.44.14: On the surface of the earth or on the ocean, on mountains and in forests, or even in the midst of Pātāla, my course is never obstructed.
t.4.44.15: Thus then, one by one, the vānaras there, made proud by their strength, spoke these words in the presence of the king of the monkeys.
